clue.text: Town in pass is instantly recognized as bird sanctuary

indicators.note: the town sits inside the run of letters across these three clue words

explanation.surface: A mountain pass is at once known as a haven for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'pass is instantly'. The rest of the clue hints at St Francis of Assisi, famous for preaching to the birds, so the town is a fitting 'bird sanctuary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisi is a hill settlement in Umbria, Italy, birthplace of St Francis.

clue.text: Tip Aesop may give is fitting

indicators.note: the letters of the fabulist's words may yield a different word once rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice from the fable-teller Aesop tends to be apt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may give' signals rearranging the eight letters of TIP AESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean suitable or well-matched to the occasion.

clue.text: "Autumnal leaves like light footfalls / Of — passing through the streets" (Shelley)

definitions.text: "Autumnal leaves like light footfalls / Of — passing through the streets" (Shelley)

parts.words: "Autumnal leaves like light footfalls / Of — passing through the streets" (Shelley)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing word is the ghostly beings whose soft steps the falling leaves resemble

explanation.surface: A line of Shelley's verse with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the lines come from Shelley's 'Ode to Naples'-era verse comparing falling leaves to the footsteps of ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank needs a plural noun for ghosts or disembodied souls, which this word supplies.

clue.text: High point of Hilton development

parts.note: reads as a hotel chain's best property, but means the remote Himalayan paradise the novelist James Hilton created in Lost Horizon

explanation.surface: The best project a hotel group has built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilton' wants to be the hotel chain; it is James Hilton, whose novel Lost Horizon invented this valley. 'High point' works literally: it lies in the mountains of Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: The valley is an imagined Himalayan utopia, so it is a high spot that the writer developed.

clue.text: Beethoven's lyricist

parts.note: the German poet whose Ode to Joy supplies the words of the choral finale of the Ninth Symphony

explanation.surface: Who wrote words for Beethoven?
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller wrote the poem An die Freude, set in the Ninth Symphony's last movement.

clue.text: Did —-? His creation was certainly not for burning

definitions.text: Did —-? His creation was certainly not for burning

parts.words: Did —-? His creation was certainly not for burning
parts.note: the gap asks whether a man of that name cooked in a pan; his creation was the play The Lady's Not for Burning

explanation.surface: Did a certain man cook? Whatever he made was not meant to go into the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright's surname is also a verb for cooking in oil, so 'Did ___?' asks if he cooked; his best-known play is The Lady's Not for Burning (1948).
explanation.definitionFit: The English verse dramatist wrote The Lady's Not for Burning, the work the clue alludes to.

clue.text: She established peace, while giving rage some points @

parts.note: ire is anger or rage
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A woman made peace even while adding a few barbs to her anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Irene (Eirene) was the Greek goddess of peace; compass points N and E are a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Eirene was the Greek goddess personifying peace, so she embodies it.

clue.text: Disraeli hero, apparently not bald

definitions.meaning: the title character of Benjamin Disraeli's 1870 novel
split in two, the name looks like '...', a full head of it

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the name as LOT + HAIR: someone with plenty on top is not bald.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli's novel is named for its young hero; divided, the name suggests abundant locks, the opposite of baldness.

clue.text: Where Shylock was rated

parts.note: 'rated' here means scolded: Shylock says Antonio has berated him many a time in the Venetian exchange

explanation.surface: The place where the moneylender's worth was assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rated' looks like valued, but in Shakespeare it means rebuked: 'Signior Antonio, many a time and oft / In the Rialto you have rated me' (The Merchant of Venice).
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock names Venice's merchants' exchange as the place Antonio abused him.

clue.text: He was aided by Merlin in the basic conception of Arthur

definitions.text: He was aided by Merlin in the basic conception of Arthur

parts.words: He was aided by Merlin in the basic conception of Arthur
parts.note: 'conception' is literal: the wizard disguised a king so he could father the future king on Igraine

explanation.surface: Someone the wizard helped shape the original idea of Arthurian legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basic conception' sounds like an author's first idea; in Malory, Merlin's magic let Arthur's father lie with Igraine, so the boy was conceived.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's father in legend was helped by the wizard to beget him.

clue.text: Settle for a later adaptation of this Beaumont piece?

definitions.text: Settle for a later adaptation of this Beaumont piece?

parts.words: Settle for a later adaptation of this Beaumont piece?
parts.note: Elkanah Settle, a Restoration dramatist, rewrote this tragicomedy by Beaumont and Fletcher in 1695

explanation.surface: Should one accept a newer reworking of a Beaumont play?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle for' looks like 'accept'; Settle is the playwright Elkanah Settle, who adapted Beaumont and Fletcher's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaumont and Fletcher's tragicomedy, subtitled Love Lies a-Bleeding, was later adapted by Settle.

clue.text: What's more, he has a non-speaking part

definitions.meaning: a film or stage performer in the background with no lines

explanation.definitionFit: The word means something additional, and also a background actor without lines.

clue.text: "He accepted Arthur, his twin brother, who was, as they put it, a short" (Patrick White)

definitions.text: "He accepted Arthur, his twin brother, who was, as they put it, a short" (Patrick White)

parts.words: "He accepted Arthur, his twin brother, who was, as they put it, a short" (Patrick White)
parts.note: the quotation has dropped a word from the idiom for being mentally slow, 'a ___ short', meaning one roof tile missing

explanation.surface: A line from Patrick White's The Solid Mandala about the twin brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in clue: the idiom 'a ___ short' (a roof tile missing) means not quite all there; the line is from White's The Solid Mandala, about Arthur Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: The roofing tile completes the Australian idiom for someone simple-minded.

clue.text: West confused by art in his twofold output

indicators.note: the letters of the two words get mixed up into a surname

explanation.surface: A writer's two-sided work mixes up West and art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges WEST and ART. J. I. M. Stewart wrote both academic novels under his own name and detective stories as Michael Innes, hence 'twofold output'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford don published literary fiction and criticism under one name and crime fiction under a pseudonym, a double career.

clue.text: British composer is into its complications

indicators.note: the letters are tangled into a new order
the needed letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A composer is caught up in its difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is into' takes TOITS from inside 'into its'; 'complications' rearranges them. Sir Paolo Tosti, Italian-born, became a British subject and was knighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Paolo Tosti, songwriter and singing master to the royal family, took British nationality.

clue.text: Some trail-blazers of Cather's creation

parts.note: Willa Cather's 1913 novel of Nebraska settlers is O ___!

explanation.surface: Early explorers invented by the American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cather's novel title names these first settlers, people who open up new territory.

clue.text: Mystery of Queen Cole. Possibly not merry, but showing articulacy

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made a puzzle of, reshuffled

explanation.surface: A riddle about Queen Cole: not merry like the king of the nursery rhyme, but well-spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mystery of' rearranges QUEEN COLE; 'Possibly not merry' plays on Old King Cole, 'a merry old soul' in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, persuasive speech is the quality of being articulate.

clue.text: He remembered Arthur Hallam

parts.note: the poet whose long elegy In Memoriam A.H.H. mourns his friend Hallam

explanation.surface: A man recalled his late friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remembered' points to the elegy In Memoriam, written for Arthur Henry Hallam, who died in 1833.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian Poet Laureate composed In Memoriam in memory of Hallam.

clue.text: Sort of leverage applied by Jane Aiken Hodge?

definitions.text: Sort of leverage applied by Jane Aiken Hodge?

parts.words: Sort of leverage applied by Jane Aiken Hodge?
parts.note: 'purchase' means leverage, and Hodge's novel is titled ___ Purchase

explanation.surface: What kind of mechanical grip did the novelist use?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leverage' is a grip or 'purchase'; Jane Aiken Hodge wrote the historical romance Savannah Purchase (1971).
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the novel's title, describing a kind of 'purchase'.

clue.text: A wind blew out of a cloud, it seems, chilling a Miss Lee

definitions.text: A wind blew out of a cloud, it seems, chilling a Miss Lee

parts.words: A wind blew out of a cloud, it seems, chilling a Miss Lee
parts.note: Poe's last poem says the wind came out of the cloud by night, chilling and killing the maiden of the title

explanation.surface: A gust from a cloud seems to have given a woman called Lee a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The lines echo Edgar Allan Poe: 'the wind came out of the cloud by night, / Chilling and killing my ___ Lee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's poem is named for the young woman, ___ Lee, whom the wind chilled.

clue.text: Some earthly colour in Bloch recital

indicators.note: the colour lies inside the composer's name and the next word

explanation.surface: A trace of earthy tone appears in a Bloch performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'Bloch recital'; 'earthly' means of the earth, as ochre is a natural earth pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigment is a yellow-brown clay used since prehistory, so an earth colour.

clue.text: Comedians revealed this background

parts.note: Graham Greene's novel The Comedians is set under Papa Doc's Caribbean dictatorship

explanation.surface: Stand-up comics exposed this backstory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comedians' is Greene's 1966 novel, not funny people; its setting is the island republic ruled by Duvalier.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's setting is that Caribbean nation, so its background is of that country.

clue.text: How Beatrice produces poniards

parts.note: Benedick says of her in Much Ado About Nothing 'She ___ poniards, and every word stabs'

explanation.surface: A woman named Beatrice brings out daggers.
explanation.walkthrough: From Much Ado About Nothing: Beatrice's words are daggers, so she utters them.
explanation.definitionFit: Her poniards are words, which she produces by talking.

clue.text: Thievish bird, perhaps, doing solitary on a rock

definitions.text: Thievish bird, perhaps, doing solitary on a rock

parts.words: Thievish bird, perhaps, doing solitary on a rock
parts.note: Golding's castaway is called ___ Martin: a thief's nickname plus a bird, stranded alone on an Atlantic rock

explanation.surface: A magpie-like thief serving time in isolation on a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thievish bird' splits into a slang word for a thief and 'Martin', the bird; William Golding's Pincher Martin is a sailor alone on a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a petty thief and the first part of the title of Golding's novel.

clue.text: Some of them, they erroneously dismiss her work as romantic nonsense

indicators.note: only part of the letters across the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Critics wrongly sneer at a woman's novels as romantic fluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' takes letters from 'they erroneously'; the clue as a whole says Georgette Heyer's Regency romances are unfairly dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the novelist Georgette Heyer, the woman the clue describes.

clue.text: Getting together with David Mamet

definitions.meaning: a meeting of people after a separation
the title of an early one-act play by the American dramatist

explanation.definitionFit: A gathering again after time apart, also the name of Mamet's 1976 play.

clue.text: Closed community for those with similar habits

definitions.text: Closed community for those with similar habits

parts.words: Closed community for those with similar habits
parts.note: 'habits' are monks' robes as well as customs, so the community wears the same clothing

explanation.surface: A gated village for people who share routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' looks like routines; it means religious robes worn by monks or nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a cloistered house of monks or nuns who wear identical robes.

clue.text: In his dream was Cardinal Newman Elgar's lyricist

definitions.text: In his dream was Cardinal Newman Elgar's lyricist

parts.words: In his dream was Cardinal Newman Elgar's lyricist
parts.note: Newman wrote the poem The Dream of ___, which Elgar set as an oratorio

explanation.surface: Someone dreamed that the cardinal wrote words for Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman's poem, set by Elgar in 1900, follows the soul of an old man; the cardinal wrote the words 'in his dream'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure is the dying man whose dream forms Newman's poem and Elgar's oratorio.

clue.text: Friend of Antonio gives sailor an unusual appearance

indicators.note: the letters show up looking strange, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A friend of a merchant makes a sailor look odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual appearance' rearranges SAILOR AN. Salarino is one of Antonio's companions in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice this gentleman is a companion of the merchant.

clue.text: Margaret Oliphant's big wheel, Catherine, saves the family bank in Hester

definitions.text: Margaret Oliphant's big wheel, Catherine, saves the family bank in Hester

parts.words: Margaret Oliphant's big wheel, Catherine, saves the family bank in Hester
parts.note: in Oliphant's novel Hester (1883) the formidable Catherine of this surname rescues the family firm

explanation.surface: A powerful woman named Catherine rescues a bank in a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Margaret Oliphant's Hester, Catherine Vernon saved the family bank and rules the town of Redborough.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the family surname of Catherine, the dominant heroine of Oliphant's novel.
